input.quote: Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party. Except for termination for material breach as detailed in paragraph 4(b), Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period regardless of which Party terminates the Agreement
input.rationale: Compliant at the fallback; no redline and no counterparty comment proposed. A Customer convenience right is present and enforceable by us. The preamble (p0000) defines The Associated Press as the "Customer" and provides that "Each of Customer and Kubient may be referred to herein individually as a 'Party'", so the Section 4(a) grant that "Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party" expressly confers a for-any-reason (convenience) exit on AP. The deterministic "Customer convenience termination present" check fails only because the sentence uses the defined term "Party" instead of naming the Customer; that is a drafting-phrasing artifact and does not affect the substance. Notice period: 90 days, squarely inside the fallback's 60-90 day window. Term: a one (1) year Initial Term auto-renewing in 1-year increments, so the trigger for "absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months" is not met and there is no multi-year lock-in. Vendor side: Kubient's convenience right requires the same 90 days' notice - not "fewer than 90 days" - so the walk-away threshold is not reached, the right is symmetric rather than one-sided against us, and the Initial Term bar prevents Kubient exiting mid-term. Economics: Kubient's entitlement to fees "generated during the termination period" is bounded by the ~3-month notice period rather than being an uncapped early-termination penalty, consistent with the fallback cap of no more than 3 months' fees, and it applies whichever party terminates. Noted per the minor sub-element rule, not flagged: 90 days rather than the preferred 30; Kubient's right not confined to term-end; and no pro-rata prepaid-fee refund, which is inapplicable because Section 5 is a revenue-share under which Kubient remits to AP rather than AP prepaying fees.
